tagline: Qatar's historic southern port town — the marine-village anchor that extends the Doha network down the coast.
summary: Al Wakrah is a historic pearling and fishing port just south of Doha, redeveloped around a restored souq, corniche and marina, with the Al Wakrah/Al Janoub stadium district and fast-growing southern suburbs behind it. It sits on the same sheltered Gulf coast as Doha, Lusail, The Pearl and Mesaieed, with calm shallow water and short hops between the corniche, the marina and the offshore developments. As Doha's water-transport network matures, Al Wakrah is the natural southern anchor — a marine-heritage town with the corniche, leisure and commuter demand to support a clean foiling tier.
competitive_landscape: Qatar's urban water transport is nascent — limited Doha Bay water taxis and tourist dhows, with no fast, clean, on-demand network linking the coastal nodes. Al Wakrah today is road-connected to Doha along a congested highway corridor, with its marina used mainly for leisure. There is no incumbent fast-ferry service to displace; the opportunity is to extend a Doha-anchored foiling network southward along a calm, build-ready coast as part of Qatar's broader waterfront and tourism push.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The southern-Qatar coastal mesh — Al Wakrah↔Doha (~9 nm), Al Wakrah↔Pearl/Lusail (~14–18 nm), Al Wakrah↔Mesaieed (~16 nm) — sits well inside the 70 nm all-electric range. Calm, shallow, sheltered Gulf water and zero local emissions suit high-frequency Pioneer II rotations off the existing marina and corniche.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The coastal network stays in Pioneer II range; Quanta-LR hybrid range would open longer Gulf line-haul (e.g. toward Qatar's offshore developments or down toward the Saudi/UAE coast) without charging dependency, integrating Al Wakrah into a wider GCC corridor.

precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates clean foiling fleets serving warm, calm, build-ready coastal geographies at scale — the same operating profile as the southern-Qatar Gulf coast.

regulatory_note: Qatar maritime activity falls under the Ministry of Transport and Mwani Qatar (ports authority), with strong state backing for tourism-and-waterfront diversification under Qatar National Vision 2030. The calm, regulated Gulf coast and government-led development of Al Wakrah's marina and corniche provide a supportive permitting environment for a clean water-transport tier.
seasonality: A winter-weighted leisure market (November–April) when Gulf temperatures are comfortable, with peak summer heat (June–September) favouring air-conditioned, low-energy electric cabins for commuter use. The sheltered Gulf is calm and navigable year-round, giving a weather-stable operating profile with only occasional summer shamal winds.
